title: Rotational spectroscopy and astronomical search for the 2-hydroxyacetonitrile isotopologues HO<SUP>13</SUP>CH<SUB>2</SUB>CN, HOCH<SUB>2</SUB><SUP>13</SUP>CN, and DOCH<SUB>2</SUB>CN
question: Measure the laboratory rotational spectra of the 2-hydroxyacetonitrile isotopologues HO13CH2CN, HOCH213CN, and DOCH2CN from 150 to 530 GHz and search for them in the ISM towards Serpens SMM1-a and IRAS16293 B.

data.sensitivity: better than 6 mJy beam^-1 for a bin width of 1 km s^-1 (IRAS16293 B ATOMIS request)

what.value: Ab initio dipole moments, ground vibrational state rotational constants, quartic centrifugal distortion constants, and vibrational band centers of hydroxyacetonitrile

evidence.quote: It is also the case of 2hydroxyacetonitrile: µ a = 2.32 D, µ b = 1.31 D, µ c = 1.23 D. These ab initio values are from Dalbouha et al. (2017).
we used as starting parameters the ab initio ground vibrational state rotational constants of Table 2 in Dalbouha et al. (2017)
The band centers values were taken from Table 3 in Dalbouha et al. (2017).

what.value: Spectroscopic parameters (centrifugal distortion, tunneling splitting, Coriolis coupling) of the main isotopologue HOCH2CN

evidence.quote: all the other parameters (centrifugal distortion, tunneling splitting, and Coriolis coupling constants) were taken from Margulès et al. (2017).
The first column of the table shows the parameters of the main isotopologue from Margulès et al. (2017).

what.value: Centimeter-wave rotational parameters and tunneling energy difference estimation for DOCH2CN

evidence.quote: The initial spectral predictions were calculated with Watson’s Hamiltonian in the I r representation, the rotational parameters from Cazzoli et al. (1973)

what.value: HOCH2CN column density, excitation temperature, line width, and V_LSR in SMM1-a and column density in IRAS16293 B

evidence.quote: Hydroxyacetonitrile was detected at N Tot = (7.4±0.9)×10 14 cm −2 , T ex = 260±45 K, ∆ V 2.5±0.3 km.s −1 , and V LSR = 6.8±0.2 km.s −1 (Ligterink et al. 2021).
Using the column density of 3×10 15 cm −2 derived for the main isotopologue by Ligterink et al. (2021), we obtain a 13 C/ 12 C ≤ 0.5.

what.value: Excitation temperature of HOCH2CN in IRAS16293 B

evidence.quote: Assuming an excitation temperature of 150 K (similar to the one obtained by Zeng et al. 2019), a source size of 0.5 ′′ , a linewidth ∆ V = 1 km s −1 , and a V LSR = 2.7 km.s −1

recipe.goal: Fit laboratory rotational spectra and generate spectroscopic line lists and partition functions
recipe.method: Least-squares fitting of measured submillimeter lines (150–530 GHz) using the Reduced Axis System (RAS) formalism and Watson's S-reduction Hamiltonian; partition functions computed from SPCAT rotational partition functions and harmonic vibrational approximations.
key_parameters: J up to 90 and Ka up to 40 for Q_rot; four lowest vibrational excited states below 870 cm^-1 for Q_vib
assumptions: Some octic distortion constants (L_K, l_2, l_3) for 13C isotopologues fixed to main isotopologue values; dipole moments taken from ab initio calculations (µ_a = 2.32 D, µ_b = 1.31 D, µ_c = 1.23 D)

recipe.goal: Search for isotopologues and derive column density upper limits in Serpens SMM1-a
recipe.method: Extract single-beam spectrum towards the SMM1-a continuum peak, search for lines above 3 S/N, and compute LTE synthetic spectra in line-free regions to set upper limits on column density.
key_parameters: T_ex = 260 K, ΔV = 2.5 km s^-1, V_LSR = 6.8 km s^-1, 3 S/N detection threshold
assumptions: Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium (LTE); T_ex, ΔV, and V_LSR fixed to main isotopologue values from Ligterink et al. (2021)

recipe.goal: Search for isotopologues and derive column density upper limits in IRAS16293 B (PILS and archival data)
recipe.method: Search for transitions at the half-beam offset position in the ALMA-PILS survey (329–363 GHz) to derive column density upper limits; query archival ALMA data at 1–2" resolution using ATOMIS and inspect archival FITS cubes.
key_parameters: PILS search: T_ex = 150 K, source size = 0.5", ΔV = 1 km s^-1, V_LSR = 2.7 km s^-1; ATOMIS query: angular resolution 1–2", spectral resolution < 0.5 km s^-1, sensitivity < 6 mJy beam^-1 per 1 km s^-1, Bands 3–6, A_ij > 5 x 10^-5 s^-1
assumptions: T_ex = 150 K, source size = 0.5", ΔV = 1 km s^-1, V_LSR = 2.7 km s^-1, and main isotopologue N = 3 x 10^15 cm^-2

score_reason: The laboratory line lists and .cat predictions are publicly hosted at CDS and LSD, and the ALMA data are public in the archive with fixed LTE parameters explicitly stated, though the astronomical results are visual upper limits and rely on companion papers for spectrum extraction details.
rediscovery_reason: All ALMA project codes are public, the spectroscopic catalogs (.cat files) and partition functions are publicly released, and the LTE parameters (T_ex, ΔV, V_LSR) used to derive the upper limits are explicitly stated.
